claim: Nine token-gated venue-truth diag routes (exchange_positions, venue_session, ib_open_orders, broker_account_status, bybit_open_orders, bybit_raw_order_history, bybit_raw_closed_pnl, bybit_raw_positions, alpaca_open_orders) answer HTTP 200 with accounts:[] (and ib_open_orders count:0) when list_accounts() raises OR when the requested account_id matches nothing, so 'could not look / wrong account id' is byte-identical to 'looked, venue holds nothing'.
evidence: MEASURED locally 2026-09-27 via fastapi TestClient on HEAD f5353c3 with DIAG_READ_TOKEN set: (a) monkeypatch src.units.ui.data_loaders.list_accounts to raise -> GET /api/diag/exchange_positions -> 200 {'requested_account_id': None, 'requested_symbol': None, 'accounts': []}; (b) list_accounts returning [] -> identical 200 body; (c) list_accounts=[{account_id: bybit_2}] and GET /api/diag/ib_open_orders?account_id=bybit_typo -> 200 {'requested_account_id': 'bybit_typo', 'count': 0, 'accounts': [] ...}. Code: src/web/api/routers/diag.py:2295-2298 `except Exception ... # allow-silent: ... returns empty accounts so the call still answers` / `accounts = []`; same pattern at diag.py:2415, 2541, 2728, 3246, 3340, 3438, 3560, 3663 (grep -n 'list_accounts failed'). list_accounts -> _load_yaml_accounts (src/units/ui/data_loaders.py:191-215) also converts a YAML parse failure into a report() + empty list without raising.
expected: A failed accounts read, and an account_id filter that matches no configured account, are reported as distinct states (e.g. accounts_read: could_not_look / unknown_account_id, count: null) — the file's own contract for ib_open_orders is 'count is null, never 0, when we could not look' (docs/api-tier-policy.md Tier 2.5 ib_open_orders row).
actual: 200 with an empty accounts list and, on ib_open_orders, count: 0.
population: All 26 routes in diag.py read; 9 of 26 call list_accounts and all 9 carry the swallow (grep count 9). 3 of the 9 reproduced by TestClient (exchange_positions x2 modes, ib_open_orders typo).
blast_radius: These are the independent venue-side surfaces audits and reviews use to prove 'no position / no resting order on the broker' (CA-A01-001 was found through ib_open_orders). A typo'd account id or an unreadable accounts.yaml yields a clean-looking negative on real-money protection questions. Read-only; no order path.
detector: test: for each of the 9 routes, monkeypatch list_accounts to raise and assert the body carries an explicit could-not-look state (not accounts:[]); and request an unknown account_id and assert a 404 or unknown_account_id state. Could be generalised as a guard flagging `accounts = []` inside an except in routers/diag.py.
proposed_fix: In each route: on list_accounts failure return 503 {'error':'accounts_unreadable'} (the file already 503s on import failure two lines above); when account_id is given and no configured account matches, return 404 {'error':'unknown_account_id'}; set count to None when no account was read. Make _load_yaml_accounts surface its errors list to callers.

claim: A critical alert (e.g. 'Account auto-paused after N consecutive exchange rejections') is popped from the in-process queue before sending, and AlertManager.send_alert swallows every send exception, so a failed Telegram send permanently drops the alert and the caller's except-branch that would log it is dead code.
evidence: READ: src/main.py:889-901 `for alert in pop_alerts(): ... try: telegram_client.send_message(...) except Exception: logger.exception('alert_drainer: telegram send failed')`; src/main.py:55-61 `_AlertManagerAdapter.send_message` -> `self._am.send_alert(message)`; src/bot/alert_manager.py:22-36 `try: ... asyncio.run(_send()) except Exception as exc: logger.warning('Alert failed: %s', type(exc).__name__)` — never re-raises, logs only the exception type name. pop_alerts is destructive (src/units/dashboards/alerts.py). Not executed against Telegram (no network send attempted by this lane).
expected: Per _drain_critical_alerts' own docstring (the 2026-05-10 'alert queued but never sent' incident), a critical alert is either delivered or its non-delivery is visible (requeued, or recorded as undelivered with cause).
actual: On any send failure the alert is gone from the queue and the only trace is a WARNING 'Alert failed: <TypeName>' in the trader log; the drainer's logger.exception branch can never fire.
population: One transport (AlertManager, the only production telegram_client per src/main.py:64-73) and one drain loop; population of critical-alert producers not enumerated by this lane.
blast_radius: Operator-notification path for account auto-pause / circuit-breaker events on the live trader; a Telegram outage or token problem silently suppresses them. No order path affected.
detector: test: make telegram.Bot.send_message raise inside AlertManager.send_alert and assert _drain_critical_alerts leaves the alert re-queued (or writes an undelivered record); assert send_alert returns/raises a distinguishable failure.
proposed_fix: Have AlertManager.send_alert return bool (or raise) and have _drain_critical_alerts re-queue alerts whose send failed (bounded retries), logging the exception message, not only its type name.
note: Code sits in src/main.py (CA-A06/A02 scope) and src/bot/alert_manager.py (this lane); reported here because the swallow is in src/bot.

claim: src/web/api/auth.py states the API is default-deny ('every route attaches Depends(require_session) unless its path is in PUBLIC_ROUTES', 'enforced ... by the test suite'), but 108 of 113 non-docs routes carry no require_session and PUBLIC_ROUTES is read by no runtime code.
evidence: MEASURED: walked the live FastAPI route tree (fastapi 0.141.1, via _IncludedRouter.original_router) and collected each route's dependency calls: require_session appears on exactly 4 routes (/api/status, /api/pnl, /api/bot/db/tables, /api/bot/db/table/{table}); 26 /api/diag/* routes use _require_diag_token in-body; the rest have no session gate. `grep -rn PUBLIC_ROUTES src tests scripts` -> only src/web/api/auth.py (definition) and tests/test_web_api_auth_login.py:159-163 (asserts membership of 4 strings). auth.py:21-24 and 150-152 carry the claim.
expected: Either the docstring describes the real model (explicit Tier-1 public reads per docs/api-tier-policy.md, which is the actual authority) or the gate is default-deny.
actual: Default-allow: a new route is public unless its author adds a gate; the only mechanical backstop is api-tier-policy-guard requiring a doc row, which does not check the row's tier against the code.
population: 113 routes under routers/ + main.py's /api/health; 4 FastAPI docs routes excluded.
blast_radius: Misleads readers of the auth module about the posture of the public, browser-reachable API; a new write route could land ungated believing a global gate exists.
detector: Extend scripts/check_api_tier_policy.py to compare each route's documented tier with its detected gate (require_session / _require_diag_token / token helpers) and fail on mismatch.
proposed_fix: Rewrite the auth.py docstring to state the real model (public by default, gates per docs/api-tier-policy.md), and either delete PUBLIC_ROUTES or make it an enforced allowlist; add the tier-vs-gate check above.

claim: docs/api-tier-policy.md and auth.PUBLIC_ROUTES document GET /, GET /login and GET /static/* as live public surfaces, but no such routes or mounts exist and the live host 404s all three.
evidence: MEASURED 2026-09-27 against https://ict-bot.duckdns.org: GET / -> 404, GET /login -> 404, GET /static/x.js -> 404. `grep -rn 'StaticFiles\|app.mount' src/web` -> no matches. docs/api-tier-policy.md:187 row '`GET /` · `GET /login` · `GET /static/*` | UI surfaces / `app.mount`'; auth.py:43-56. `python3 scripts/check_api_tier_policy.py --list` itself prints them as 'documented endpoint(s) with no route'.
expected: Inventory lists only routes that exist.
actual: Three phantom routes documented as Tier 1.
detector: Make check_api_tier_policy fail (not advise) on documented endpoints that exist neither under routers/ nor in main.py.
proposed_fix: Delete the row and the three PUBLIC_ROUTES/PUBLIC_PREFIXES entries (keep /api/health).

claim: docs/api-tier-policy.md contradicts itself on route counts: the machine-checked banner says '113 of 113' while the same sentence says the enumerator 'finds exactly those 96'; the Tier-2.5 section says 'all 16 routes on this router call _require_diag_token' while diag.py has 26; and GET /api/diag/bybit_wallet_truth has two rows.
evidence: docs/api-tier-policy.md:22 ('113 of 113'), :25 ('exactly those 96'), :274-275 ('all 16 routes'), :287 and :297 (two bybit_wallet_truth rows). `grep -c '^@router\.' src/web/api/routers/diag.py` -> 26; `grep -c '_require_diag_token(' diag.py` -> 27 (26 calls + def).
actual: Three stale hand counts beside the checked one.
population: Whole doc (338 lines) grepped for counts.
detector: Only the banner is test-checked (TestStatedCoverageIsTrue); no detector for prose counts is practical — delete the prose counts instead.
proposed_fix: Remove '96' and '16', merge the duplicate row.

claim: docs/reference/bot-api-reference.md § CORS lists the allowed origins as localhost:5173, localhost:3000 and DASHBOARD_ORIGIN, omitting the hardcoded https://benbaichmankass.github.io and WEBAPP_ORIGINS — the only origin the live SPA uses — and does not state allow_methods=[GET, POST].
evidence: docs/reference/bot-api-reference.md:312-316 vs src/web/api/main.py:61-79 (`_origins.append("https://benbaichmankass.github.io")`, WEBAPP_ORIGINS CSV, `allow_methods=["GET", "POST"]`). MEASURED live: GET /api/bot/stats with Origin github.io -> access-control-allow-origin: https://benbaichmankass.github.io; OPTIONS preflight from https://evil.example -> 400 with no allow-origin (correct).
expected: Doc lists every allowed origin and the method allowlist.
actual: Doc omits the load-bearing origin and methods.
blast_radius: Doc accuracy; runtime CORS is correct.
detector: A test asserting every origin literal in main.py appears in the doc's CORS section.
proposed_fix: Add github.io + WEBAPP_ORIGINS + methods/headers to the doc section.

claim: DELETE /api/bot/devices/{id} and PATCH /api/bot/devices/{id}/subscriptions are documented as consumer-facing (bot-api-reference labels them Tier 1) but CORS allow_methods=[GET, POST] refuses them browser-direct, and their only client (Android) is retired, so the routes have no possible browser consumer while remaining fail-open anonymous writes if DASHBOARD_API_TOKEN is ever unset.
evidence: MEASURED live: OPTIONS /api/bot/devices/1 with Origin github.io and Access-Control-Request-Method: DELETE -> 400, access-control-allow-methods: GET, POST. GET /api/bot/devices unauthenticated -> 401 'missing authorization' (so DASHBOARD_API_TOKEN IS set on the live VM today; the fail-open is latent). src/web/api/routers/devices.py:67-84 `_check_admin_token` returns silently when the env is unset; used at :302, :339, :381. docs/reference/bot-api-reference.md:175-176 'Tier 1'.
expected: Write routes fail closed like prop/report and work/decision (BL-20260705-DASHBOARD-API-TOKEN-UNSET), or are removed if nothing can call them.
actual: Fail-open gate on two write routes no consumer can reach.
blast_radius: One push-token row per call; no money path. Latent while the token is set.
detector: test: with DASHBOARD_API_TOKEN unset, DELETE/PATCH must return 503.
proposed_fix: Switch devices writes to the fail-closed helper (or delete the routes); fix the doc tier label.

claim: The two unauthenticated Tier-1 write carve-outs write into trade_journal.db with no row cap, no rate limit and no request-size limit, and POST /api/bot/learning/progress accepts a resource_id primary key of unbounded length, so an anonymous caller can grow the live money DB file without bound.
evidence: READ: src/web/api/routers/learning.py:266-268 `resource_id = str(body.get('resource_id') or '').strip()` (no length cap; note is capped at :276 `[:2000]`), upsert via sqlite3.connect(_resolve_db_path()) at :183-184; devices.py:45,221 caps token at 4096 but has no row cap. src/web/api/main.py: no body-size middleware (only CORSMiddleware). Not exercised live (a write probe would mutate production).
expected: docs/api-tier-policy.md Tier-1 rule 3: 'safe to expose to anyone who can reach the API' under the threat model 'the dashboard URL leaked to a hostile party'.
actual: Unbounded anonymous growth of the file the live trader journals into.
population: 2 unauthenticated write routes (all of them, per the route walk).
blast_radius: Disk exhaustion on the live VM's journal volume would stop trade journaling; requires a hostile caller.
detector: test: POST learning/progress with a 1 MB resource_id must 400; guard: every unauthenticated POST route must declare max lengths.
proposed_fix: Cap resource_id length (e.g. 200) and validate it against the curriculum's known ids; cap device_tokens rows; consider moving learning_progress out of trade_journal.db.

claim: GET /api/bot/config's secret-key denylist (which docs/api-tier-policy.md says is 'what keeps this Tier 1') does not match passphrase, private_key, webhook/webhook_url, auth_key, pin or bearer, and its test only uses key names the regex already matches, so it cannot catch the gap.
evidence: src/web/api/routers/bot_config.py:112-116 `_SECRET_KEY_PATTERN = re.compile(r"(api[_-]?key|api[_-]?secret|secret|token|password|passwd|signing[_-]?key|hash|credential)", re.I)`. Executed by the reader: 'passphrase', 'private_key', 'webhook_url', 'auth_key', 'pin_code', 'bearer' -> no match. tests/test_web_api_bot_config.py:217 fixture keys (api_key, api_secret, BYBIT_TOKEN, password, passwd, signing_key, credential_blob, user_hash, inner_secret, another_api_key) all contain a pattern literal. `grep` of config/strategies.yaml found no such key today -> latent.
expected: Redaction covers common secret spellings; test fixtures derived from a spec list, not from the regex.
actual: Six common spellings pass through unredacted on an unauthenticated route.
blast_radius: Would publish a strategy-param credential to the internet if one is ever added. Nothing leaking today.
detector: Parametrised test over a curated secret-name list (passphrase, private_key, client_secret, webhook_url, auth, bearer_token, pin, cert, keystore).
proposed_fix: Extend the pattern (passphrase|private[_-]?key|webhook|auth|bearer|pin\b|cert|keystore) and share one helper with strategies.py (see next finding).

claim: GET /api/bot/strategies serves each strategy's raw strategies.yaml block as `config` with no redaction, while docs/api-tier-policy.md:178 states 'secrets are not in this surface' and the sibling /api/bot/config treats redacting the same file as load-bearing.
evidence: src/web/api/routers/strategies.py:98-107 `_load_strategies_yaml` returns the parsed dict; :438 `"config": cfg,`; no call to bot_config._redact_recursive or any denylist in the file (grep). docs/api-tier-policy.md:178.
expected: One shared redaction applied to every route serving strategies.yaml.
actual: Safety holds only because no key is secret-shaped today.
detector: Guard: any router loading config/strategies.yaml must pass it through the shared redactor.
proposed_fix: Apply bot_config._redact_recursive (after widening it) in strategies.py.

claim: Several unauthenticated reads return HTTP 200 with an empty result when the underlying read FAILED, indistinguishable from 'nothing there': /api/bot/order-packages (sqlite error -> rows:[],count:0), /api/bot/strategies (yaml load error -> strategies:[]), /api/bot/strategy/attribution (sqlite error -> []), /api/bot/logs and /api/bot/signals (OSError -> []), /api/diag/audit (OSError -> []), and /api/diag/status + snapshot.status (corrupt runtime_status.json -> null, same as never-written).
evidence: READ: order_packages.py:245-253; strategies.py:98-107 (except Exception -> return {}); attribution.py:197-199; dashboard.py:477-495 and 498-532 (self-labelled 'S-067 borderline'); diag.py:1139-1161 (_audit_tail, also 'S-067 borderline') served at :1793-1796; diag.py:1122-1136 (_status_json_payload). Contrast: trades_closed.py docstring 'IT NEVER RETURNS A BARE [] TO MEAN SOMETHING WENT WRONG'; bot_config.py surfaces config_load_errors for the same yaml.
expected: Each route returns an explicit read state (or 503) on a failed read, per CLAUDE.md 'a count that reads 0 may mean we could not look' and scripts/ci/check_collapsed_states.py.
actual: 7 routes serve a clean-looking empty on failure.
population: 7 routes identified across the 5 readers' slices; not an exhaustive sweep of all 113 routes.
blast_radius: Operator-facing dashboard and diag reads show 'no activity' during an outage; no order path.
detector: Register these fields with check_collapsed_states CONTRACTS; per-route tests forcing the failure branch.
proposed_fix: Add a read_state/error field (or 503) on each failure branch, following trades_closed.py.

claim: /api/bot/notifications drops the alert-severity banners (trainer down, broker account down, prop fills stale) when their detector raises, logging only at DEBUG, so a broken detector reads as 'all clear' — while sibling detectors in the same file emit an explicit 'cannot be measured' banner.
evidence: src/web/api/routers/notifications.py:91-93 (`except Exception ... logger.debug(...); return None`), :253-255 (account-down), :259-305 (prop fills stale); contrast _losing_streak_banners :308-372 and _starved_account_banners :375-431 which branch on *_UNREADABLE.
expected: A detector failure yields a visible 'status unknown' banner.
actual: Banner silently omitted; DEBUG log only.
population: 5 banner detectors in the file; 3 collapse.
blast_radius: Operator's safety banner feed; no order path.
detector: test: monkeypatch each detector to raise and assert a *_unknown banner is returned.
proposed_fix: Emit a warning-severity '<kind> status unknown' banner on exception and log at WARNING.

claim: The Telegram comms handler replies 'Recorded ... ✅' to the operator even when the git writeback push (the only path by which the answer reaches the repo) raised GitPushError, and nothing retries the push.
evidence: src/bot/comms_handler.py:645-661 (apply_answer catches GitPushError, logs error + log_event, returns normally); :531 and :586 send 'Recorded' unconditionally after apply_answer. Reader: `grep -rn commit_and_push src` -> one call site. Whether the comms request channel carries live traffic today was not established.
expected: Operator told when the answer did not propagate; failed push retried.
actual: False success reply; answer stranded on the VM.
blast_radius: Operator decisions answered via Telegram may never reach the repo.
detector: test: patch GitPusher.commit_and_push to raise; assert the reply differs from the success reply.
proposed_fix: Return push outcome from apply_answer; reply with a warning on failure; retry pending pushes from CommsPoller.

claim: In the same ict-telegram-bot process, the menu gate fails closed when TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID is unset but the comms answer gate fails open ('unconfigured -> don't break tests/dev'), letting any chat answer operator decision prompts under that misconfiguration.
evidence: src/bot/comms_handler.py:443-458 `if allowed is None: return True`; src/bot/telegram_query_bot.py:120-127 is_authorised compares to TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID and fails closed. Both installed in telegram_query_bot.main() (install_comms_handlers). A WARNING is logged at registration.
blast_radius: Requires the env to be unset; then any Telegram user can answer prompts.
detector: test: _chat_authorized with comms_allowed_chat_id=None must return False outside an explicit test flag.
proposed_fix: Fail closed; tests set the chat id explicitly.

claim: POST /api/auth/login returns 403 for a non-allowlisted email and 401 for a wrong password (email oracle), verifies against an unsalted single-round SHA-256, and has no attempt throttling; latent because the live host returns 500 auth_unavailable.
evidence: src/web/api/routers/auth.py:45-56; src/web/api/auth.py:97-104 (sha256 hexdigest compare). MEASURED live 2026-09-27: POST /api/auth/login {email: a probe address, password: x} -> 500 {'error':'auth_unavailable'}.
expected: Uniform 401 on any bad credential; slow salted hash; rate limit.
blast_radius: Only once auth envs are set on the VM (prerequisite for Tier 2a).
detector: test asserting identical status/body for wrong-email and wrong-password.
proposed_fix: Return 401 for both; move to a KDF (scrypt/argon2) hash env; add per-IP throttle — do this before setting the envs.

claim: /ws/market is unauthenticated with no connection cap, and each connection polls up to 12 symbols every 2 s through the single-worker candle executor and the single-worker account-read executor shared with REST /candles and /positions (and IB pacing).
evidence: src/web/api/routers/market_ws.py:57-116 (_POLL_SECONDS=2.0, _MAX_SYMBOLS=12, no counter); candles._FETCH_EXECUTOR and _account_read_executor.py max_workers=1. Not load-tested.
blast_radius: Dashboard read latency / IB pacing under many connections; no order path.
detector: Test that the (N+1)th connection is refused.
proposed_fix: Global connection cap (e.g. 4) and per-IP cap.

claim: Eight async diag routes call list_accounts() (synchronous open + YAML parse of accounts.yaml, uncached) directly on the event loop, which check_async_route_blocking cannot see because it only flags direct sqlite3/subprocess/time.sleep/requests calls.
evidence: diag.py:2295, 2413, 2539, 3244, 3338, 3436, 3558, 3661 (`accounts = list_accounts() or []` inside async def); src/units/ui/data_loaders.py:191-200; scripts/ci/check_async_route_blocking.py:54-59.
expected: All blocking I/O in async routes offloaded.
actual: Small local-file read on the loop.
blast_radius: Milliseconds per call; the guard's clean result overstates coverage.
detector: Extend the guard with a list of known-blocking helpers (list_accounts).
proposed_fix: Wrap list_accounts in run_account_read/to_thread or cache it.

claim: src/bot/recurring_dispatch.py and src/comms/templates.py describe Telegram commands (/audit, /improve_strategy, /train_model, /roadmap, /new_session, /test) that no CommandHandler registers; their functions have only test callers.
evidence: Reader grep of every CommandHandler( registration in telegram_query_bot.py, claude_bridge.py, claude_decision_bot.py: none of those commands. recurring_dispatch.py:1-18, templates.py:1-18; claude_bridge.py:8-10 records the removal. log_trigger/build_starter_prompt/make_new_session_request callers: tests only.
detector: None practical beyond a docstring review; the dead functions can be deleted instead.
proposed_fix: Delete the dead functions or mark the modules as archived.

claim: tests/test_menu.py's kill-switch keyboard tests skip whenever python-telegram-bot is not installed, which requirements-test.txt makes the default, so the callback_data for killacct/killstrat buttons is never asserted in standard CI.
evidence: tests/test_menu.py `_kb_callbacks` returns [] when markup has no inline_keyboard and callers pytest.skip; requirements-test.txt:83-85 leaves python-telegram-bot out; tests/conftest.py:42-72 stubs telegram with MagicMock.
blast_radius: A regression in kill-switch callback strings would pass CI.
detector: A CI job with python-telegram-bot installed, or build the callback strings in a pure function and test that.
proposed_fix: Extract callback_data construction into a pure helper and test it without telegram.
